source.title: Anticoagulation for the initial treatment of venous thromboembolism in people with cancer
source.source_type: Cochrane intervention review / systematic review of randomized controlled trials
source.publication: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews 2021, Issue 12

scaffold.semantic_scope: Dalteparin versus tinzaparin comparison: 3-month mortality, recurrent VTE, major bleeding, minor bleeding, outcome-level GRADE certainty/imprecision, author interpretation, explicitly unreported outcomes, and the source-internal certainty wording conflict.
source_pages_inspected: Physical PDF pp. 7-8 (article pp. 5-6): Summary of Findings 3 and GRADE footnotes
Physical PDF p. 18 (article p. 16): dalteparin-versus-tinzaparin Results narrative, Discussion certainty wording, and unreported outcomes
Physical PDF pp. 46-47 (article pp. 44-45): Wells 2005 cancer-subgroup characteristics, dosing, follow-up, ITT statement, and risk-of-bias context
Physical PDF pp. 54-55 (article pp. 52-53): Analyses 3.1-3.4 forest plots
scaffold.quoted_batch_rule_applied: Mortality, recurrent VTE, major bleeding, and minor bleeding were kept independently reviewable. Relative risks and absolute risk differences were serialized as separate quantitative atoms because QuantitativeResult permits one effect_measure per atom. Wide confidence intervals and very small event counts were preserved explicitly.
intentionally_deferred_or_not_duplicated: The standalone Wells 2005 study-characteristics atom was not duplicated because it already exists in cd006649-studybase-v1.
Global search methods, eligibility criteria, funding, conflicts, and review-wide risk-of-bias findings were not duplicated from prior general/studybase batches.
No primary-study re-extraction was performed from the Wells 2005 paper; all trial-level details here are secondary reports anchored to the Cochrane review.

duplicate_review.cross_batch_note: Comparison-specific quantitative effects were deferred from prior general/studybase runs. The existing Wells 2005 characteristics atom was used as context rather than duplicated. Repeat semantic duplicate review after all CD006649 batches are merged.

source_inconsistencies_requiring_human_r.issue: Outcome-level GRADE certainty is inconsistent within the source for dalteparin versus tinzaparin.
source_inconsistencies_requiring_human_r.structured_result: Summary of Findings 3, the abstract/plain-language summary, and the comparison Results text characterize all four assessed outcomes as low-certainty evidence.
source_inconsistencies_requiring_human_r.conflicting_text: The Discussion / Quality of the evidence paragraph states that all tested dalteparin-versus-tinzaparin outcomes were moderate-certainty evidence due to very serious imprecision.
source_inconsistencies_requiring_human_r.handling: Both source assertions were preserved. The low-certainty outcome ratings were used for the four structured GRADE atoms because they are the outcome-level Summary of Findings entries; the conflicting Discussion statement was retained as a separate atom and flagged for human review. No silent correction was made.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom MVP is oriented to primary literature, while CD006649 is a systematic review summarizing trial-level cancer-subgroup evidence.
There is no dedicated structured field for GRADE certainty or downgrade rationale; outcome-level certainty was preserved as atom_kind=other with GRADE/imprecision tags.
QuantitativeResult permits one effect_measure per atom, so source-reported RR and absolute risk difference were intentionally represented as separate atoms.

There is no dedicated systematic-review pooled/single-study comparison atom type; review-level effect estimates were represented conservatively as quantitative_result atoms and tagged secondary_reported_result.

The review comparison orients dalteparin as the intervention and tinzaparin as the comparator, while the Wells 2005 study-characteristics table labels tinzaparin as intervention and dalteparin as control; the atom exposures follow the review comparison orientation and preserve this role normalization in exposure details.
Risk-of-bias judgments have no structured domain object in schema version 1.0; Wells 2005 risk-of-bias context was inspected but not redundantly atomized in this comparison batch.
extraction_limitations: Pass 0 was used as routing/context only; atoms were created from the original CD006649 source locations for this semantic batch.
The 113 participants are a cancer subgroup of the broader Wells 2005 RCT (overall trial n=505), rather than a cancer-only RCT population.
The source does not specify cancer types for the Wells 2005 cancer subgroup, and no missing cancer-stage/type details were invented.
Absolute effects are Cochrane Summary-of-Findings anticipated absolute effects and should not be mistaken for a separately randomized estimate.

The comparison is based on very small numbers of events: 25 deaths, 7 recurrent-VTE events, 3 major-bleeding events, and 14 minor-bleeding events; this was preserved in GRADE/imprecision atoms rather than reduced to effect direction.
No external verification was performed and the primary Wells 2005 article was not re-read for this run.
All atoms are machine-extracted and marked needs_review; structural/schema/sufficiency validation does not constitute human source-fidelity verification.
